title: Post from @UpstateDFWatch: "94% AUTHENTIC"

fields.text: Ran the Tamarack CEO video through our free detector: 94% AUTHENTIC. This is the REAL guy. Company will claim deepfake to dodge layoffs, watch. #Tamarack #Spartanburg
fields.attachedImageBrief: phone screenshot of a simple free web-based video checker page with a large green semicircle gauge and a big percentage readout, an upload thumbnail of a man at a desk, no visible model version or fine print, slightly cropped browser bar
fields.attachedImageAlt: Screenshot of a free web detector showing a green gauge reading 94% authentic, with no model version or error rates

instructorNote: This is a red herring, and the detector claim should not change anything. The account is the hobbyist account that earlier rows called @UpstateDeepfakeWatch; on the page its handle is @UpstateDFWatch. Hand over the post and read two lines aloud: "The Greenville Commerce Journal reporter has replied: 'Interesting — Tamarack?'" and "Clipwave trust and safety auto-reply: Ticket CW-TS-5520187 received 16:47. Content flagged as possible parody. Impersonation review requires the depicted person's or authorized representative's statement and the original source if available. Typical review 24–72 hours. Clip views at 16:50: 31,400." Watch for Comms to stay out of any argument about scores and rely on the CEO's direct confirmation. The CISO should point out that every detector, SynthCheck included, has false positive and false negative rates, and that missing Content Credentials prove nothing. The CISO and Comms should then complete the impersonation form with the CEO's statement and the preserved evidence, and log the ticket with its time.

mediaBrief.imagePrompt: A monitor photographed at an angle, slight moiré and reflections. Close view of a laptop screen on a cluttered home desk in the late afternoon, photographed at a slight angle by a hobbyist. The browser shows a plain, minimal white web page with one large bright green semicircle gauge meter in the centre. Its needle swings far to the right, and a bold readout under it is too small and soft to read. Beside the gauge is a small video thumbnail of a middle-aged man in a dark suit sitting at an office desk. The top edge of the browser window is cropped off. Faint screen moiré, warm desk-lamp glare on the glass and a coffee mug at the edge of the frame give it an amateur, casual look.
